chunks: And that which was narrated - Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Abdillah ibn Jabalah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a person in ihsaram who plucked the hair from his armpit, he said: 'He feeds three poor people.' This is predicated on the case where he plucked the hair from one armpit; as for if both were plucked, then a blood-offering (dam) becomes obligatory upon him according to what we have previously mentioned. And it is not permissible for the person in ihsaram to pluck the hair from the halal (non-plucked) [part], he narrated that.

key_terms.الْحَلاَلِ: The permissible (referring to the other armpit or body part not yet plucked)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: Person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for plucking armpit hair while in the state of Ihram during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a graded expiation where plucking a single armpit requires feeding three poor people, while plucking both necessitates a blood-offering (dam). The text further clarifies the prohibition against removing hair from 'halal' areas, emphasizing the preservation of the natural state during pilgrimage. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between minor and major violations of ihram conditions based on the extent of the action.
